name: Iona Batchelder, Director
bio: Cellist Iona Batchelder is a passionate artist and teacher who is deeply committed to fostering a genuine environment of music-making for performers, audiences, and students of all ages.

Recent collaborations include a performance with actor Rainn Wilson at the New York Times Climate Forward Event, an appointment as guest lecturer of cello at the University of California, Irvine, and recital appearances on Lincoln Center’s The Art of Wellbeing series. Ms. Batchelder is a section cellist in the Princeton Symphony Orchestra and has performed with the New York City Ballet, Orpheus Chamber Orchestra, New Jersey Symphony Orchestra, the American Symphony Orchestra, Orchestra Lumos, and the New York Classical Players.

Ms. Batchelder was a founding member of the Unison Quartet, which won an Honorary Mention award at the 2021 Bartók World Competition in Budapest, Hungary. She has performed at several festivals including Kneisel Hall, the Perlman Music Program, and the Aspen Music Festival. Always curious to explore different genres and styles of music, Ms. Batchelder has made main stage appearances with a wide variety of artists including Andrea Bocelli, Jon Batiste, Sofia Carson, and Judy Collins, and has also participated in score recording work on Netflix’s “Green Eggs and Ham.”

Ms. Batchelder was a proud recipient of a Kovner Fellowship at The Juilliard School, where she graduated with her Bachelor of Music and Master of Music degrees, both under the tutelage of Darrett Adkins, and a Juilliard Career Advancement Fellowship. She studied chamber music with artists including Joel Smirnoff, Roger Tapping, Joel Krosnick, Daniel Druckman, and Joseph Kalichstein. Deeply committed to educating the next generation, Ms. Batchelder maintains a private studio in New York City and teaches at Suzuki on the Island in Manhasset, NY.

name: Ariel Horowitz
bio: Ariel Horowitz is a violinist, composer/songwriter, and educator whose work bridges performance, teaching, and community-engaged practice. Hailed by The Washington Post as “sweetly lyrical,” she maintains an active national and international career as a soloist and chamber musician, performing repertoire that spans the Western classical canon alongside original compositions, songwriting, and improvisation. She is currently represented worldwide by Bright Shiny Things.

As a performer, Horowitz appears regularly as a soloist, chamber musician, and collaborator in a wide range of contexts, from traditional concert halls to interdisciplinary and community-centered venues. She performs with ensembles including Sybarite5, Vision Duo, and Jupiter Symphony Chamber Players, and has appeared at venues such as Joe’s Pub, Merkin Hall, the Kennedy Center Millennium Stage, and the Strathmore Center for the Arts.

Horowitz is also a dedicated educator, and has held faculty appointments at Mount Holyoke College and the Chamber Music Center of New York, where she coaches pre-college chamber music ensembles. She is the Founder and Artistic Director of the Heartbeat Music Project, a tuition-free music education and Diné cultural education program serving Navajo youth. Heartbeat operates by invitation and in deep collaboration with Diné elders, educators, and knowledge keepers, with cultural and language programming led by community-based leadership. Through this work, Horowitz leads interdisciplinary teams of artists and educators and engages in culturally responsive practice grounded in listening, respect, and shared ownership.
Horowitz holds degrees from Yale School of Music and The Juilliard School, where her primary teachers included Ani Kavafian, Itzhak Perlman, and Catherine Cho.

name: Emma Frucht
bio: Violinist Emma Frucht is celebrated for her fearless leadership, warmly expressive playing, and collaborative spirit that inspires fellow musicians and audiences alike. A dedicated orchestral leader, Emma is co-concertmaster and a core Chamber Ensemble member of the Orchestra of St. Luke’s in New York City. She performs regularly in leadership positions with the New York Classical Players, East Coast Chamber Orchestra, A Far Cry, Orpheus Chamber Orchestra, The Oratorio Society of New York, and Musica Sacra, and is a recurrent guest with the American Ballet Theater Orchestra.

A native New Yorker, Emma completed her undergraduate studies at Harvard University, majoring in Art History. Shortly after earning her Master of Music degree from the Juilliard School, Emma joined the Grammy-nominated Aizuri Quartet. A member of the Quartet from 2019-2025, notable highlights from her time in the group include the quartet’s major concerto debut with the Milwaukee Symphony Orchestra performing John Adams’s Absolute Jest, their debuts at the 92Y , Carnegie Hall, and Boston’s Celebrity Series, and Chamber Music America’s Cleveland Quartet Award.

Emma relishes any chance to collaborate with living composers, finding great joy in the process of bringing their works to life. She has participated in numerous premieres, most recently including the world premiere of George Meyer’s Concerto for Two Violins and Viola with the New York Classical Players, a string quartet by Jennifer Higdon commissioned for the Buffalo Chamber Music Society’s 100th Anniversary, and leading the Carnegie Hall premieres of new symphonic works by Billy Childs and Joe Hisaishi as concertmaster.

name: Isabella Geis
bio: Violinist and teaching artist Isabella Geis is an active chamber, orchestral, and solo musician based in New York City. She holds Master's and Bachelor's degrees from The Juilliard School, where she studied under Naoko Tanaka and David Chan.

Isabella has performed extensively across the United States in cities such as Atlanta, Aspen, Detroit, and Cincinnati. Recently, she has frequently collaborated with the Orchestra of St. Luke’s and The Knights, appearing at prestigious venues including Radio City Music Hall, Carnegie Hall, and the Elbphilharmonie Hamburg. Additionally, she has been featured as a soloist at New York Fashion Week and returns annually to The Aspen Institute to perform Bach’s Chaconne for the Henry Crown Fellowship program.

Deeply committed to education and community engagement, Isabella served as a teaching fellow for Juilliard's CLIMB (Combining Literacy Instruction with Musical Beginnings) program and as a Morse Community Engagement Teaching Artist. Through the latter, she began her extensive work with The Harmony Program, bringing music instruction to schools throughout the Bronx and Manhattan. Today, Ms. Geis continues her passion for education by teaching violin to over one hundred elementary and middle school students at the Washington Heights and Inwood Music Community Charter School (WHIN).

name: Jennifer Ahn
bio: Jennifer Ahn is an Omaha-raised, NYC-based violinist whose dynamic career has taken her across North America, Europe, and Asia. With a passion for performance, she has appeared at international venues including Carnegie Hall, Suntory Hall, the Holland Performing Arts Center, and the Athens Conservatoire. She made her solo debut with the Omaha Symphony at age 11 and has since performed with all major orchestras in Nebraska, as well as the Ottawa Chamber Symphony, Malibu Coast Chamber Orchestra, and the Manhattan School of Music (MSM) Chamber Orchestra. Most recently, she appeared with the New York Youth Symphony (NYYS) on its summer tour to Greece.

An engaging and enthusiastic artist, Ms. Ahn has been featured in MSM’s Centennial Celebration Concert Series and has performed with the Chamber Music Society at Lincoln Center, the Seven Hills Chamber Music Festival, and the Annapolis Chamber Music Festival. She has also participated in the Brian Lewis Young Artist Program, the Heifetz Institute, the Pacific Music Festival, and the Music Academy of the West, where she was named the winner of the inaugural Duo Competition. Her 2025–2026 performance season includes appearances with the New York Classical Players, the Princeton Symphony, and the Frisson Ensemble.

Ms. Ahn’s passion for music began at the Omaha Conservatory of Music (OCoM), where she studied with Ruth Meints. She earned both her Bachelor’s and Master’s degrees from MSM under the tutelage of Pinchas Zukerman and Patinka Kopec, while also serving as a studio assistant and cultivating her interest in teaching. Her commitment to education is reflected in her work as a Teaching Artist with the New York Pops’ PopsEd program, as a mentor for NYYS, and through her private studio. She has also served as a guest artist faculty member at OCoM and has helped students gain admission to music programs across the country.

name: Hannah Burnett
bio: New York-based freelancer, Hannah Burnett, began playing viola at the age of three. A native of Waco, Texas, she has performed internationally, with concerts at prestigious venues like Carnegie Hall and the Royal Concertgebouw. Hannah serves as the Principal Violist of the Washington Heights Chamber Orchestra and is a member of the New York Classical Players and the Princeton Symphony Orchestra. She is frequently invited to play with NOVUS Trinity, the American Ballet Theater orchestra, and Riverside Symphony. An avid chamber musician, she has spent summers at Kneisel Hall and Yellow Barn Festivals and was a founding member of the Unison Quartet, whose successes brought them to the Juilliard String Quartet Seminar, quartet residencies at the Perlman Music Program and the Aspen Center for Advanced String Quartet Studies, and the finals of the 2021 Bartok World Competition in Budapest. Hannah has been coached by members of the Juilliard String Quartet, and has collaborated with artists such as Natasha Brofsky, Anthony Marwood, Gilbert Kalish, Krzysztof Chorzelski, Janine Jansen, and Donald Weilerstein. In addition to her active performance career, she serves on the faculty of the Greenwich Suzuki Academy and maintains a small private studio in the city. Hannah holds two degrees from Juilliard, where she studied with Roger Tapping and Misha Amory and was a recipient of the Kovner Fellowship.

name: Samuel DeCaprio
bio: Cellist Samuel DeCaprio is a dynamic performer and teacher based in the Tri-State area. Among his numerous honors, he received a Norman Benzaquen Career Advancement Grant from The Juilliard School, won the Aldo Parisot Prize at the Yale School of Music and the prestigious Performer's Certificate from the Eastman School of Music, along with top prizes from the Arlington, Eastern Connecticut Symphony, National Federation of Music Clubs, and William C. Byrd competitions. His New York debut featured the North American premiere of Grażyna Bacewicz’s Cello Concerto No. 2 with the Juilliard Orchestra and conductor David Robertson in Alice Tully Hall. Appearing across the globe as a soloist and chamber musician, he has been featured on prominent radio programs including WQXR New York, WFMT Chicago, NPR, and WCNI, and has recorded for Delos, ECM Records, MSR Classics, and Nonesuch Records. He has played as a substitute with the New York Philharmonic, New York City Ballet, and Princeton Symphony Orchestra.

A passionate chamber musician, DeCaprio’s festival appearances include Ravinia Steans Music Institute, IMS Prussia Cove Open Chamber Music, Les Rencontres Musicales de Noyers-sur-Serein, Domaine Forget, Kneisel Hall, Lake George, Meadowmount, and Orford Musique, and collaborated with renowned artists, including Atar Arad, Paul Biss, Natasha Brofsky, Steven Doane, Vladimir Feltsman, Joseph Lin, Daniel Phillips, David Shifrin, Barry Snyder, and Irma Vallecillo. In 2022, DeCaprio founded the Arazzo Music Festival—an annual chamber music festival focused on bringing free high-caliber concerts and educational events to his home state of Connecticut. DeCaprio holds degrees from UConn, Eastman, Mannes, Yale, and Juilliard. His principal teachers include Joel Krosnick, Aldo Parisot, Marcy Rosen, Steven Doane, and Kangho Lee.

name: Joanne Kang
bio: Dr. Joanne Kang is a New York-based Australian pianist and teaching artist praised for her “fleet-fingered virtuosity” and stylistic versatility. A prizewinner of national and international competitions and scholarships, she maintains an active career as a soloist, chamber musician, and recording artist, and is regularly engaged to perform national and world premieres.

Joanne has collaborated with artists and ensembles including the American String Quartet, The Afield, American Modern Opera Company, West Australian Symphony Orchestra, Julia Wolfe, members of the Silk Road Ensemble, and the late Kaija Saariaho, for whom she performed the world premiere of Semafor, the composer’s final chamber work. From 2020–2023, she was pianist of Carnegie Hall’s Ensemble Connect, hailed as “one of the strongest ensembles in the city” (New York Classical Review). She has appeared on major stages and for organizations including Rocket City New Music, Philadelphia Chamber Music Society, Chamber Music Society of Central Virginia, Ballet Fantastique, Carnegie Hall, Lincoln Center, the Guggenheim Museum, Sydney Opera House, Seoul Arts Center, National Sawdust, and Salle Bourgie, among others.

Joanne earned her Bachelor, Master, and Doctor of Musical Arts degrees from the Manhattan School of Music, where she received the Harold Bauer Award and Helen Cohn Award. As assistant to the late Prof. Phillip Kawin and a Doctoral Teaching Fellow in the Keyboard Skills Department, she taught undergraduate and graduate keyboard skills, individual piano lessons, and studio classes. From 2020–2024, she also held teaching residencies at Skidmore College through Ensemble Connect, providing private instruction and chamber music coaching.

Her recordings include albums 1Q84 (ODDSOUND Records, 2024) and i wish i were dead with Duo Étrange (ATMA Classique, 2026). An upcoming release features cello and piano works by New York composers Gene Pritsker and Randall Woolf (Composers Concordance Records/Naxos).

name: Zhu Wang
bio: Praised as “especially impressive” and “a thoughtful, sensitive performer” who “balanced lyrical warmth and crisp clarity”(Tommasini–The New York Times), Chinese pianist Zhu Wang has won the 71st Maria Canals International Piano Competition of Barcelona, receiving the Fundació Occident Prize in March 2026. He was awarded First Prize in the 2020 Young Concert Artists Susan Wadsworth International Auditions, Gold Medalist at 2024 New Orleans International Piano Competition. Zhu was one of the finalists in the 2019 Clara Haskil International Piano Competition, and the prize of Audience Favorite during the Opening Play-off and Female Composer Prize of 2024 Cleveland International Piano Competition. The world-renowned pianist Fou Ts’ong recognized Zhu as an “excellent pianist with a natural sense of harmony and imagination,” whose sensitive and engaging performances exhibit a remarkable depth of musicianship and poise.

An avid chamber musician, Zhu has appeared on series such as Chamber Music Detroit, Bridgehampton Chamber Music Festival, Vancouver Recital Society, La Jolla Music Society, Stanford Live, Hamilton College, Four Seasons Chamber Music Festival, Howland Chamber Music Series, Chesapeake Music, Clarion Concerts, Philadelphia Chamber Music Society,  and Chamber Music Society of Lincoln Center. Zhu is an alum of Kneisel Hall Chamber Music School, Bravo! Vail, Caramoor’s Evnin Rising Stars, Music@Menlo International Program, and he regularly appears in chamber music recitals with violinist Randall Goosby.

A native of Hunan Province, China, Zhu started learning piano at the age of five following his grandfather’s love of music. Zhu is a graduate of Curtis Institute of Music and The Juilliard School and received Gina Bachauer Scholarship, Mieczyslaw Munz Scholarship, and Mehlin Prize. His mentors are Robert McDonald, Mikhail Voskerensky, Emanuel Ax, Angela Hewitt and Zhe Tang. He gratefully acknowledges the support of the Bagby Foundation for the Musical Arts. Zhu currently lives in New York City with his wife Chloe and their beloved three cats, Chaz, Tùzi and Juzí.

name: Pascal Archer
bio: Hailed by The New York Times as “an outstanding clarinetist,” Pascal Archer leads an active career as a performer and teacher.

He is the founder and artistic director of Exponential Ensemble, a chamber music ensemble that creates educational programs and commissions new works connecting music with math, science, and literacy. He has collaborated with the JACK and St. Lawrence String Quartets, the North Country Chamber Players, Orpheus Chamber Orchestra, and Camerata Pacifica, and has toured with Musicians from Marlboro.

Since 2006, Pascal has been principal clarinetist of the NEPA Philharmonic. During his tenure with the orchestra, he has served as a board member and chamber music coordinator and founded the NEPP Mentoring Program. He is also principal clarinetist of the Glimmerglass Festival Orchestra and Princeton Symphony Orchestra.

A former member of the New World Symphony, he has served as Acting Principal Clarinet of the New Jersey Symphony for three seasons and as a guest clarinetist with the Metropolitan Opera Orchestra. He has performed in the orchestras of numerous Broadway productions, including Sweeney Todd, Mary Poppins, South Pacific, On the Town, Fiddler on the Roof, and My Fair Lady. He has also performed at renowned music festivals including Mostly Mozart, Mostly Modern, Verbier, Spoleto USA, Marlboro, and Sun Valley Summer Symphony.

Mr. Archer is on the faculty of the Manhattan School of Music Precollege, Fordham University, and Hunter College. Additionally, he coaches chamber music at the Chamber Music Center of New York and the Alaria Chamber Ensemble.
Originally from Québec, Mr. Archer holds degrees in music performance from the Conservatoire de Musique de Montréal, Université de Montréal, Indiana University, and the Manhattan School of Music.
In his free time, Pascal enjoys swimming, great meals with friends, and traveling to warm destinations.
